title: Maria Montessori's birth chart
metaDescription: Maria Montessori's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 7.8° Virgo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: 0.2° separates Mars and Uranus from an exact conjunction; at that range drive and disruption read as one mechanism. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 7.8° Virgo — deep enough in the first decan (0°–10°) that Mercury, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 3.5° Libra, Venus at 12.9° Leo, Mars at 24.7° Cancer. Mercury in a air sign reads as thought that travels by comparison; Venus in a fire sign reads as attraction declared rather than implied; Mars in a water sign reads as effort that surges when it matters.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mars to Uranus, a conjunction with 0.2° of slack. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct. Behind it, Saturn trine Neptune at 0.5°, and Jupiter opposition Saturn at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: The Sun makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags three placements in this chart. The Moon in Scorpio at 9.7° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Cancer at 24.7° is in fall; Jupiter in Gemini at 23.4° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 3 in water, 3 in fire, 2 in earth, 2 in air by element, 4 cardinal, 3 mutable, 3 fixed by modality. A water emphasis reads as porousness: the room is registered whole, long before it is analysed in parts. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Scorpio for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 14.5° between midnight and midnight. The sign survives the missing hour; the degree does not, and is given as a reference rather than a fact. At the noon reference it stands at 9.7°.
